AUTHOR: Saleh
TITLE: A realistic fish-habitat dataset to evaluate algorithms for underwater visual analysis
REGION: Tropical Australia (mostly Hinchinbrook/Palm Islands, NE Queensland; some Western Australia)
SPECIES: Fish (no species labels); juvenile fish assemblages
DATA: DeepFish (own; derived from Bradley et al. 2019 habitat survey videos)
V_EV: Data collection: 'Video recording were carried out during daylight hours, and in relatively low turbidity periods.' (restricted to low turbidity, not measured)
D2: 50/20/30 per habitat, balanced fg/bg (FishClf 19883/7953/11930; FishLoc 1600/640/960; FishSeg 310/124/186)
D_EV: Dataset splits: 'We randomly select 50% training, 20% for validation and 30% for testing for each habitat while ensuring that the number of background and foreground images are equal'
R_EV: Dataset splits: splits aggregated from each habitat of the single DeepFish dataset; 'we aggregate the selected training images from each habitat into one training split'
C_EV: Localization results: 'the predicted probability map are thresholded to become 1 if they are larger than 0.5 and 0 otherwise.' (default threshold, no sensitivity/FP analysis)
E_EV: Counting results: 'The counting model with the backbone pretrained on ImageNet achieved an MAE of 0.38 ... an average of 0.38 fish miscounts per image'
ARCH: ResNet-50 backbone + FFN (classification/counting), FCN8 + LCFCN loss (localization), FCN8 + focal loss (segmentation)
NOTE: V_ALL=N per policy P1 (recording restricted to 'relatively low turbidity periods' without measurement). Depth was measured with an acoustic sounder but values are not reported (V2=NR). V3=Y from 'daylight hours'. D: random image split within each habitat, frames from the same videos likely in all splits; leakage not discussed. E1: per-image count MAE against human point annotations of the same images coded as 사람 계수와 비교 (E_ALL=P); a verifier may consider this a pure benchmark metric (E1=없음, E_ALL=N). C: LCFCN 'false-positive loss' is a training loss, not FP evaluation.
